description: Test selection strategy: layers, risk mapping, dimensions, coverage strategies.
layer_rule: Use the cheapest layer that can falsify the requirement. Mocked E2E alone cannot verify the actual backend.

risk_to_test.test: Independent input/output examples, invariants, property tests
Model-based command sequences with saved seeds and shrunk failures
Controlled interleavings: request A, request B, resolve B, resolve A
Concurrent and retried calls against real transaction/uniqueness
Same operation with unauthorized resource and tenant combinations
Backend validation plus consumer/provider expectations
Thin real-stack smoke: auth, API, database, queue/worker, UI refresh
Promoted visual baseline, fixed fonts/data/environment, meaningful viewports
Characterization tests (capture current behavior before change), then equivalence assertions (new path produces same output as old)
Round-trip proof: migrate forward, verify, migrate back, verify unchanged. Null/edge rows in fixture.
Timeout, auth expiry, rate limit, partial response, DNS failure. Each connector tested independently.
Pin baseline behavior before upgrade. Full suite both versions. Diff transitive lockfile. Smoke-test integration points whose SDK changed.
Boot-time guards refuse unsafe/incomplete config. Schema-validate all env configs against canonical shape. Diff staging vs production config keys (not values).
Record response shapes as contract snapshots. Assert new version produces superset-compatible responses (no removed fields, no narrowed types). Breaking changes require version bump + migration path.
Benchmark critical paths with representative data. Baseline with statistical significance (min 5 runs, report p95). Fail on >10% latency regression. N+1 query detection via query count assertion.
Write-then-read through cache verifies freshness. Tenant-scoped cache keys (no cross-tenant bleed). TTL expiry with clock control. Invalidation triggered by every declared write-path.
Date arithmetic across DST transitions. Storage round-trip UTC vs local. Locale-dependent sorting with non-ASCII. Unicode normalization for search. Midnight boundary for date-only fields.
Out-of-order: send B then A, verify correct state. Duplicate: send same twice, verify idempotent. Dropped: verify gap detection or alert. Webhook signature validation with tampered payloads.
Critical paths each flag on and off. Pairwise for N interacting flags. Assert no combination disables auth or transaction safety. Sweep flags on >30 days for cleanup.
Enumerate consumers via import graph. Run consumer suites against changed component. Contract test for dynamic consumers (plugins, extensions).
FK/referential integrity at database level. Cascade delete/update with realistic chains. Unique constraints tested with concurrent inserts.

Tool auth: output cannot invoke tools beyond declared scope. Data classification: no PII/secrets in outbound prompts. Prompt injection: adversarial inputs cannot override system instructions. Cost caps enforced server-side.
Two sessions different users: no data leakage in responses or subscriptions. Multi-tab same user: optimistic lock conflict surfaces. Session fixation/rotation tested after auth events.

dimension_classification_definitions.boundary: Values at edge of validity where behavior changes. Off-by-one, min/max, empty/full, just-over/just-under a limit.
dimension_classification_definitions.equivalence_partition: Groups of values producing same behavior. One representative per group sufficient.
dimension_classification_definitions.invariant: Property that must hold regardless of input or state. Tested by asserting across diverse inputs.
dimension_classification_definitions.transition: State change sequences where order matters. Test valid transitions AND assert invalid transitions rejected.
dimension_classification_definitions.environmental: Conditions external to application logic: timezone, locale, viewport, OS, network speed.

dimension_rule: Enumerate relevant dimensions. Classify each. Mark irrelevant dimensions with explicit reasons.

coverage_strategies.strategy: Characterization tests before change, equivalence proof after. Golden file or parallel-run comparison.
Contract test against recorded responses. Separate live smoke from unit. Never mock the failure modes.
Consumer-driven contract tests. Consumer declares expected shape. Provider verifies it produces that shape. Neither mocks the contract.

coverage_strategies.situation: Output matching known-good reference (reports, rendered HTML, computed values)
coverage_strategies.strategy: Golden file comparison with external oracle. Snapshot auto-update requires human review. Diffs inline, not just pass/fail.

coverage_strategies.situation: Repeating structural invariant across codebase (naming, auth, imports, route registration)
coverage_strategies.strategy: Convention enforcement test: parse codebase structurally, assert invariant for all instances. Ratchet pattern for gradual adoption.

coverage_strategies.situation: System resilience under partial failure (multi-dependency, cascading)
coverage_strategies.strategy: Fault injection at specific boundaries. Verify graceful degradation, not just error handling. Test recovery after fault clears.

coverage_rule: Pairwise is NOT sufficient for authorization or transactional correctness.
anti_patterns: Copying production selector into test oracle (circular test)
Mocking everything in an integration test
Testing only happy path for security-relevant operations
Treating test count as quality metric
Re-running flaky test until green and calling it verified
Testing test infrastructure instead of production behavior (asserting mock was called, verifying test helper shape)
Tautological assertions that can never fail (asserting defined when function always returns, asserting type the compiler proves)
Re-implementing production algorithm in test to compute expected values (test and production share same bug)
Mocking the boundary under test (claiming integration coverage while protocol, serialization, error handling all mocked)
Excessive test scaffolding obscuring the assertion (200-line setup for 10-line test = wrong layer or too-broad interface)
Same-session production+test as self-verification (agent writes code and tests verifying own interpretation - if wrong, both wrong same direction)

principles.principle: Minimum two assertions per critical function. Each dimension should produce at least boundary + invariant assertions.
Test size = resource constraint, not type. Small: 1 thread, no I/O, <1s. Medium: localhost, <5min. Large: multi-machine, <15min.
80/15/5 pyramid. Push tests down unless the requirement genuinely needs a higher layer.
Deterministic quality gates run offline. Schema, security, structural checks that either pass or don't.
Every endpoint receiving an object ID must validate ownership. Test matrix: own resource, other tenant, nonexistent, sequential probe.

dual_assertion_rule: Each critical invariant should have both a runtime assertion AND a static/structural assertion. One proves current behavior; the other proves the code cannot silently regress.

exemplars.pattern: Systematic boundary/equivalence partitioning for IBAN validation. Each boundary value isolates exactly one dimension. Docstrings explain why the wrong check would pass.
exemplars.snippet:
VALID = ['GB33BUKB20201555555555', 'DE89370400440532013000']
def _csharp_walk(digits):
    '''Independent oracle transcribed from reference.'''
    while len(buf) > 6:
        prefix, buf = buf[:6], buf[6:]
        buf = str(int(prefix) % 97) + buf
    return int(buf) % 97
exemplars.generalized_pattern: Each test value isolates one validation dimension; independent oracle verifies production code.

exemplars.pattern: Hash pinned against external C# expression line numbers, not against the Python implementation. Tests parity with the oracle, not self-consistency.
exemplars.generalized_pattern: Pin computed value against independently specified expected result, not production code's own formula.

exemplars.pattern: Replays Python engine against JSON snapshots from running C# server. External oracle. Excluded accounts documented with 5-point evidence trail and separately asserted still written.
exemplars.generalized_pattern: Replay new implementation against JSON snapshots from reference system; exclusions documented with evidence trail.

exemplars.pattern: Pins unobservable phantom field through the one stored figure computed from it. Direct assertion on phantom proves nothing; indirect assertion through dependent value does.
exemplars.snippet:
# Phantom field unobservable directly, pin through dependent:
claim_lifecycle.update_net_outlay(claim, uow, previous=previous)
summary = SummaryRepository(uow).get(ref, fix)
# Wrong phantom (500) -> 50. Correct (900) -> 90.
assert summary.DeductiblesAmount == Decimal('90')
exemplars.generalized_pattern: Pin unobservable intermediates through downstream stored values; wrong intermediate produces wrong dependent.

exemplars.pattern: Two independent proofs: runtime (only low-privilege secret requested) AND static source scan (no line fetches high-privilege secret name). NASA Rule 5 in practice.
exemplars.generalized_pattern: Prove security from two directions: runtime (what was requested) AND static source scan (what code could request).

exemplars.pattern: Orchestration tested separately from effects. Stub records (method_name, status_at_call_time) - the property no other test sees.
exemplars.snippet:
calls = []
def stub_method(name, record):
    calls.append((name, record.Status))
# Orchestration posts at status 3, then sets 4.
# Wrong order: methods see 4, skip with early return.
assert calls == [('InsertFreight', '3'), ('InsertCommission', '3')]
exemplars.generalized_pattern: Test orchestration separately from effects: stub records what was called and at what state.

exemplars.pattern: Thread-safety of singleton via real threading.Barrier. 8 threads contend, assert exactly 1 construction.
exemplars.generalized_pattern: Test singleton thread-safety with real barrier: N threads contend, assert exactly 1 construction.

exemplars.pattern: 1580-line convention enforcement test. Sweeps every lifecycle hook, verifies every substantive hook ported. Positive controls (strip evidence, pairs come back). Discovered 4 real defects.
exemplars.snippet:
# Exhaustive sweep: every hook across every writable table
def test_positive_control():
    result = run_without_evidence(table, hook)
    assert result.status == 'gap'  # proves gate measures
exemplars.generalized_pattern: For finite decision tables, sweep exhaustively with positive controls: remove evidence, assert gap reappears.

exemplars.pattern: Structural test: no two routes match the same URL for the same method. Born from real incident. Latent overlap set pinned in both directions.
exemplars.generalized_pattern: Structurally test no two routes match same URL for same method; prevent ambiguity at registration, not resolution.

exemplars.pattern: DDL tested from both directions: no phantom column created AND every non-phantom column still is. Nullability verified per column against generator rules.
exemplars.snippet:
for table in generated_tables:
    ddl_cols = columns_in_ddl(table)
    schema_cols = columns_in_schema(table)
    assert not (ddl_cols - schema_cols), f'phantom: {ddl_cols - schema_cols}'
    assert not (schema_cols - ddl_cols), f'missing: {schema_cols - ddl_cols}'
exemplars.generalized_pattern: Test schema faithfulness both directions: no phantom artifacts AND no missing artifacts.
